P-BEST: PP-Based Designs and Clinical Context

Muhammad Yaseen

2026-09-26

Source: vignettes/ppgt_pbest.qmd

1 Abstract

This vignette distinguishes the standard PP-based 48-pool P-BEST family from the later clinical P-BEST discussion. It also separates paper-aligned matrix content from the package-specific helpers that live around the P-BEST design family.

2 The Standard PP-Based P-BEST Family

The standard PP-based P-BEST matrix family in the package is generated by pp_matrix(q = 8, d = 3, nl = 6, N = 384), which gives \(J = 48\) pools for \(N = 384\) individuals.

At the matrix level, this is a PP design with \[ q = 8, \qquad d = 3, \qquad n_l = 6, \qquad N = 384, \] so the full PP identity \[ J = n_l q = 48 \] matches the standard 48-pool family used in the package documentation.

This constructor call gives the package’s PP-based 48-pool design family. The key structural features are:

  • \(N = 384\) individuals
  • \(J = 48\) pools
  • each individual appears in six pools
  • each pool contains 48 individuals in the standard package configuration

4 Structural Summaries 

Matrix::rowSums(M_pbest)[1:8]
  [1] 48 48 48 48 48 48 48 48
Matrix::colSums(M_pbest)[1:8]
  [1] 6 6 6 6 6 6 6 6

The displayed column sums show \(w_i = 6\). The row sums show the realized pool sizes \(n_j\).

5 Matrix-Family Alignment Versus Protocol Claims

The matrix call above is the package’s reference-aligned claim for the PP-based 48-pool family. That claim is narrower than saying that the package reproduces every protocol, decoder, or laboratory workflow associated with later P-BEST variants.

  • Matrix-family alignment: the structural PP-based 48-pool construction represented by pp_matrix(q = 8, d = 3, nl = 6, N = 384)
  • Package decoding: pp_comp() and pp_decode() are package decoding helpers built around the matrix interface
  • Clinical package helpers: package-specific objects such as pbest_clinical_matrix() are documented as separate package functionality

This distinction matters because a pooling matrix is only one layer of a full testing protocol. The matrix-level claim concerns the design \(\mathbf{M} \in \{0,1\}^{48 \times 384}\) and its PP structure. Laboratory workflow rules, Ct-based interpretation, retesting policies, and stage-2 follow-up belong to different layers.

7 Distinguishing The 48-Pool Family From Later Clinical P-BEST

The 2020 P-BEST references and the later 2024 clinical P-BEST work should not be conflated.

  • The 48-pool PP-based family is the Reed-Solomon / PP-based configuration represented in the package by pp_matrix(q = 8, d = 3, nl = 6, N = 384).
  • The later clinical discussion concerns higher-capacity operational designs, workflow choices, Ct-based interpretation, and clinical deployment issues.

The package therefore keeps two separate stories:

  • a PP-based matrix family story for the 48-pool algebraic design
  • a clinical package-helper story for later operational high-capacity layouts

8 Package-Specific Boundary

The matrix constructor above is the paper-aligned PP-based configuration. The package also provides higher-level helpers around P-BEST-style workflows.

  • pp_decode() is a package decoding pipeline.
  • pbest_clinical_matrix() is a package clinical-design constructor.

These helpers are package functionality. They are not blanket claims that the package reproduces every stage of each P-BEST workflow exactly.

9 Package-Specific Clinical Constructor 

clinical_design <- pbest_clinical_matrix()
